one_liner: Rust distributed streaming broker with a Kafka-style topic/partition log and in-broker WASM transforms; vendor bench shows 1.4-1.56x Kafka producer throughput.
what_it_does: Fluvio is a distributed event-streaming engine: a Streaming Controller (SC) manages cluster metadata and Streaming Processing Units (SPUs) store and serve partitioned, replicated, append-only topic logs. Clients (Rust crate `fluvio`, Python, Node; community Go/Java/Elixir) produce and consume through Fluvio's own protocol, and the `fluvio` CLI plus `fvm` version manager runs a local or Kubernetes cluster. It is not Kafka wire-compatible, so Kafka clients do not work against it; Kafka is reachable only through inbound/outbound connectors. WASM 'SmartModules' can filter, map or aggregate records inside the broker on the produce or consume path.
how_it_is_fast: The design is Kafka-style: each SPU appends encoded record batches to segment files (1 GiB default) with a memory-mapped offset index, and unfiltered consumer fetches are served as file slices through sendfile(2) zero-copy (future-aio zero_copy.rs, Linux and macOS). Producers batch client-side (16 KiB batches, 0 ms linger by default, optional gzip/lz4/snappy/zstd). The vendor attributes the gap to Rust with no JVM or garbage collector rather than to a new algorithm, and the post also reports about 50 MB idle RAM versus about 1 GB for Kafka.
when_to_use: Greenfield streaming where you control both producers and consumers and do not need the Kafka wire protocol or its ecosystem

Edge or small-footprint nodes (ARM boards, Graviton, Apple Silicon) where a JVM broker's roughly 1 GB idle memory is too much; the installer ships static musl builds for Linux x86_64/aarch64 plus armv7/arm
Rust services that want an async client crate and in-broker WASM filtering/mapping instead of running a separate stream processor
Single-partition producer ingest of medium (~5 KB) records, where default configs reportedly gave 1.4-1.56x Kafka's MB/s
when_not_to_use: Existing Kafka estates: there is no Kafka wire protocol (a Kafka-protocol implementation was discontinued, and requests #3870 and #4259 closed as stale), so Kafka clients, Streams, Connect and tooling do not carry over
If you need a trustworthy tail-latency comparison: the vendor's 20-38x P99 figures compare different measured intervals (see gotchas)

Replicated production clusters sized from these numbers: the only published comparison is single-node, one partition, RF=1 on a laptop and a 4-vCPU VM, and no promised bare-metal or RF=3 follow-up appears on the vendor blog

Long-term support needs: the last stable release is v0.18.1 (2025-07-04), later commits are mostly dependency bumps, and the README says installs temporarily need the dev FVM channel while builds move from InfinyOn to fluvio-community
Native Windows servers: the README recommends WSL2

integration.form: crate (client `fluvio` on crates.io) plus prebuilt broker/CLI binaries installed via fvm
integration.dependencies: tokio (async-std-based fluvio-future before June 2025), wasmtime for SmartModules, rustls or openssl for TLS, nix/libc; Kubernetes optional (local cluster mode exists)
integration.min_toolchain: Workspace pins Rust 1.93.0 via rust-toolchain.toml and uses edition 2024 (so Rust 1.85 or newer); the crate declares no rust-version
integration.platforms: Linux x86_64/aarch64 (musl), armv7/arm gnueabihf, macOS; Windows via WSL2 recommended; sendfile zero-copy path only on Linux and macOS
integration.thread_safety: Not documented in the files read; the client is async (Tokio) and the benchmark shares a TopicProducerPool across tasks
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same topic/partition/offset model and a Kafka-like batch format, but a different wire protocol, clients and ops tooling; Kafka interop only through connectors

gotchas: The latency reported by `fluvio benchmark` comes from the producer callback, which records `created_at.elapsed()` before the produce request goes to the SPU (partition_producer.rs, same at the Jan-2025 commit 38535375 that the post used). It is therefore per-batch batching/queueing time and excludes the network round trip and broker ack, while kafka-producer-perf-test times each record from send() to its ack callback. The headline 5.8 ms vs 132 ms P99 is not like-for-like.

Storage flush tuning is effectively dead code: FlushPolicy (flush_write_count/flush_idle_msec) is marked unused, and write_batch does a blocking write on the async task followed by an async flush(). No fsync, sync_data or sync_all appears in the storage crate files read, so durability rests on the page cache plus replication.
Running a SmartModule on the consume path turns off zero-copy: batches are read into memory, run through WASM, then re-encoded (stream_fetch.rs).

The benchmark tool builds every record in memory before sending (issue #4464, open), so large --num-records runs can exhaust RAM. File-descriptor leaks on topic delete with replicas (#4465) and SPU thread growth under long runs (#2215, open) are also reported.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose Fluvio over Redpanda when you want a small Rust broker with in-broker WASM transforms and do not need Kafka API compatibility; Redpanda speaks the Kafka API and publishes far more detailed tail-latency data. Choose it over Walrus or Woodpecker when you need a networked multi-client broker with partitions, replication and consumers, not an embedded WAL or a log-storage layer.
verified_claims_summary: In InfinyOn's own Feb 2025 post, kafka-producer-perf-test.sh and `fluvio benchmark producer` each sent 200,000 5,120-byte records to a single local broker at default configs with unstated 'latest' Kafka/JVM/Fluvio versions. Fluvio reached 394.6 vs 240.95 MB/s (1.56x) on an M1 Max MacBook Pro and 190.8 vs 130.77 MB/s (1.39x) on an EC2 c7g.xlarge (Graviton, 4 vCPU). The quoted P99 latencies (5.8 vs 132 ms and 10.8 vs 419 ms) come from two tools that time different intervals, and Kafka's figures include JVM warm-up.
status_note: Apache-2.0 with about 5.3k stars and commits through May 2026, but effectively in community maintenance after moving from InfinyOn to fluvio-community: the last stable release is v0.18.1 (July 2025) and recent commits are mainly dependabot and clippy fixes. It is usable as a crate plus prebuilt binaries, not something you vendor.
